source.text: הַֽלְלוּ יָ֨הּהוֹד֣וּ לַיהוָ֣ה כִּי־ט֑וֹב כִּ֖י לְעוֹלָ֣ם חַסְדּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Praise Yah. Give thanks to YHWH, for [he is] good, for to forever [is] his loyal love.

en.L: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}. Give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, for [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is] good, for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love [is] forever.
en.B: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! Give {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} thanks, for {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is good; {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love lasts forever.
en.R: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}! Thank {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is good! His faithful love lasts forever.

decisions.choice: a psalm of confession that closes Book Four
decisions.reason: The Hebrew gives this psalm no title; it opens and closes with "Praise Yah". It retells the years from Egypt to the exile as Israel's unfaithfulness and God's patience, the other side of Psalm 105, and ends Book Four of the Psalms (verse 48).

The cry "Hallelu-yah" is a command to a group, "praise", with Yah, the short form of the divine name YHWH (as in Exodus 15:2). It is rendered "Praise the LORD", with Yah as the alternative for the name.

decisions.choice: a song of the temple: 1 Chronicles 16:34
decisions.reason: "Give thanks to the LORD, for he is good; his loyal love is forever" is a refrain of Israel's worship (1 Chronicles 16:34; 2 Chronicles 5:13; Ezra 3:11; Psalms 107:1; 118:1; 136:1). The song in 1 Chronicles 16 also ends with verses 47-48 of this psalm.
The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment to his people that does not give up (5:8).
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

source.text: מִ֗י יְ֭מַלֵּל גְּבוּר֣וֹת יְהוָ֑ה יַ֝שְׁמִ֗יעַ כָּל־תְּהִלָּתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Who can utter [the] mighty deeds of YHWH, [can] make heard all his praise?

en.L: Who can utter the mighty deeds of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, [or] make all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} praise heard?
en.B: Who can put into words the mighty deeds of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} or tell out all the praise {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} deserves?
en.R: No one can find words for all the great things {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done. No one can praise {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} enough.

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer "no one"
decisions.reason: The question means that no one can tell all that God has done; yet the psalm goes on to tell part of it.
The word (gevurot) is acts of power, here God's acts in Israel's history (145:4).
Readable states the answer the question expects (m1).

source.text: אַ֭שְׁרֵי שֹׁמְרֵ֣י מִשְׁפָּ֑ט עֹשֵׂ֖ה צְדָקָ֣ה בְכָל־עֵֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: How blessed [are] those who keep justice, [the one] who does righteousness at every time.

en.L: How blessed [are] those who keep justice, [the one] who does righteousness at every time!
en.B: How blessed are those who hold to justice and do what is right at every moment!
en.R: Life is truly good for people who are fair to others and always do what is right.

decisions.choice: How blessed: how good is the life of
decisions.reason: The word ('ashre) is a cry about the good life of those described (1:1).

decisions.choice: those who keep, the one who does
decisions.reason: The first word is plural and the second singular; both describe the same people, anyone who lives this way.

decisions.choice: justice and righteousness: fair and right dealing
decisions.reason: The two words (mishpat, tsedaqah) belong together: doing what is right and fair toward others, as God requires (Genesis 18:19). The rest of the psalm shows how Israel failed to do so.

source.text: זָכְרֵ֣נִי יְ֭הוָה בִּרְצ֣וֹן עַמֶּ֑ךָ פָּ֝קְדֵ֗נִי בִּישׁוּעָתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Remember me, YHWH, with [the] favor of your people; visit me with your salvation,

en.L: Remember me, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, with the favor of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people; visit me with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} salvation,
en.B: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, think of me when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} favor {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people; come to me with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} saving help,
en.R: {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, remember me too when {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are good to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people. Come and save me as well.

decisions.choice: me: the singer speaks for himself
decisions.reason: In verses 4-5 the singer prays for himself to share in the good God will do for his people. The ancient Greek translation has "us" here.

decisions.choice: the favor of your people: the favor you show them
decisions.reason: "Favor" (ratson) is the goodwill God shows; "of your people" means toward them.

decisions.choice: visit: come to act on someone's behalf
decisions.reason: The verb (paqad) is used of God coming to help his people (Genesis 50:24; Exodus 3:16).

decisions.choice: come to me (B); Come and save me (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what God's visit means (m3).

source.text: לִרְא֤וֹת׀בְּט֘וֹבַ֤ת בְּחִירֶ֗יךָ לִ֭שְׂמֹחַ בְּשִׂמְחַ֣ת גּוֹיֶ֑ךָ לְ֝הִתְהַלֵּ֗ל עִם־נַחֲלָתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: to see the good of your chosen ones, to rejoice in the joy of your nation, to boast with your inheritance.

en.L: to look on the good of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} chosen ones, to rejoice in the joy of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} nation, to glory with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} inheritance.
en.B: so that I may see the good things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} give {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} chosen ones, be glad with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} nation in its gladness, and give glory together with the people who belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: Then I will see {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do good things for the people {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} chose. I will be happy with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} nation and proudly praise {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} with {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own people.

decisions.choice: your inheritance: Israel, God's own people
decisions.reason: The people are God's inheritance, the possession that belongs to him (Deuteronomy 9:29; 28:9).
The verb (hithallel) is to boast; here, to boast in what God has done, as in 105:3.

decisions.choice: so that I may (B); Then I will (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has three infinitives, "to see ... to rejoice ... to glory"; Balanced and Readable make them the purpose of the prayer in verse 4.

source.text: חָטָ֥אנוּ עִם־אֲבוֹתֵ֗ינוּ הֶעֱוִ֥ינוּ הִרְשָֽׁעְנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: We have sinned with our fathers; we have done wrong; we have acted wickedly.

en.L: We have sinned with our fathers; we have done iniquity; we have acted wickedly.
en.B: Like our ancestors, we have sinned; we have gone astray and done what is evil.
en.R: We have sinned, and so did our ancestors. We have done wrong. We have done evil things.

decisions.reason: The same three verbs make the confession in Solomon's prayer for exiles (1 Kings 8:47; compare Daniel 9:5).

decisions.choice: with our fathers: like them and together with them
decisions.reason: The people confess that they share their ancestors' sin; the rest of the psalm tells the ancestors' story.
"Fathers" here means the forebears of the people, men and women; Balanced and Readable say "ancestors".

source.text: אֲב֘וֹתֵ֤ינוּ בְמִצְרַ֨יִם׀לֹא־הִשְׂכִּ֬ילוּ נִפְלְאוֹתֶ֗יךָ לֹ֣א זָ֭כְרוּ אֶת־רֹ֣ב חֲסָדֶ֑יךָ וַיַּמְר֖וּ עַל־יָ֣ם בְּיַם־סֽוּף׃

records.literal_gloss: Our fathers in Egypt did not consider your wonders; they did not remember the abundance of your loyal loves, and they rebelled at [the] sea, at [the] Sea of Reeds.

en.L: Our fathers in Egypt did not understand {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonders; they did not remember the abundance of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love, and they rebelled by the sea, at the Sea of Reeds.
en.B: Our ancestors in Egypt did not take {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} wonders to heart; they did not remember how great {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} loyal love was, and at the sea, the Red Sea, they rebelled.
en.R: Our ancestors in Egypt did not understand the amazing things {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} did. They forgot the many times {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} had shown them {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} faithful love. They turned against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} at the Red Sea.

decisions.reason: With Pharaoh's army behind them, the people said to Moses, "Were there no graves in Egypt?" (Exodus 14:10-12).
The verb (hiskil) is to have insight; they saw the wonders without grasping what they meant.
The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment to his people that does not give up (5:8).

decisions.choice: loyal loves: many acts of loyal love
decisions.reason: The plural means the many times God had shown his loyal love.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Reeds: the sea Israel crossed, known as the Red Sea
decisions.reason: The name (yam suf) means "sea of reeds". It is the sea of the crossing (Exodus 15:4, 22). The ancient Greek translation calls it the Red Sea, the name long used for it.
Balanced and Readable use the familiar name, as in Exodus; Literal translates the Hebrew name, "Sea of Reeds".
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

source.text: וַֽ֭יּוֹשִׁיעֵם לְמַ֣עַן שְׁמ֑וֹ לְ֝הוֹדִ֗יעַ אֶת־גְּבוּרָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he saved them for the sake of his name, to make known his might.

en.L: Yet {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saved them for the sake of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name, to make known {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} might.
en.B: Still {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rescued them, for the honor of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name, to show how mighty {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is.
en.R: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saved them anyway, to protect the honor of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name and to show {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power.

decisions.choice: for the sake of his name: for his own honor
decisions.reason: God's name is his reputation among the nations. He saved Israel not because they deserved it but to show who he is (Exodus 9:16; Ezekiel 36:22).
At the sea God said he would gain glory over Pharaoh, and the Egyptians would know that he is the LORD (Exodus 14:4, 18).
The simple "and" here joins God's rescue to Israel's rebellion; the sense is "yet".

source.text: וַיִּגְעַ֣ר בְּיַם־ס֭וּף וַֽיֶּחֱרָ֑ב וַיּוֹלִיכֵ֥ם בַּ֝תְּהֹמ֗וֹת כַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he rebuked [the] Sea of Reeds, and it dried up, and he led them through the deeps as [through] the wilderness.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rebuked the Sea of Reeds, and it dried up, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led them through the deeps as [through] the wilderness.
en.B: He spoke sharply to the Red Sea, and it went dry; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought them over the deep places as if across open country.
en.R: He ordered the Red Sea to dry up, and it did. He led them through the deep water as if they were walking on dry ground.

decisions.reason: God's rebuke drives back the waters (18:16; 104:7); the sea obeys as a servant does.
The LORD drove the sea back with an east wind and made it dry ground, and Israel went through (Exodus 14:21-22; compare Isaiah 63).
The word (midbar) is open land where flocks graze; they went through the sea as easily as over open ground.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Reeds: the sea Israel crossed, known as the Red Sea
decisions.reason: The name (yam suf) means "sea of reeds". It is the sea of the crossing (Exodus 15:4, 22). The ancient Greek translation calls it the Red Sea, the name long used for it.
Balanced and Readable use the familiar name, as in Exodus; Literal translates the Hebrew name, "Sea of Reeds".

source.text: וַֽ֭יּוֹשִׁיעֵם מִיַּ֣ד שׂוֹנֵ֑א וַ֝יִּגְאָלֵ֗ם מִיַּ֥ד אוֹיֵֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: And he saved them from [the] hand of [the] one who hated, and he redeemed them from [the] hand of [the] enemy.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saved them from the hand of the one who hated [them], and redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.
en.B: He rescued them from the power of the one who hated them and set them free from the enemy's grip.
en.R: He saved them from the one who hated them. He set them free from their enemy's power.

decisions.choice: redeemed: freed, as by a kinsman
decisions.reason: The verb (ga'al) is the act of a relative who buys back a family member or land. God promised to redeem Israel from Egypt (Exodus 6:6; 15:13).

decisions.choice: the one who hated, the enemy: Pharaoh and his army
decisions.reason: Both words are singular, the enemy as one; Pharaoh and his army are meant.
To be in someone's hand is to be in his power.

source.text: וַיְכַסּוּ־מַ֥יִם צָרֵיהֶ֑ם אֶחָ֥ד מֵ֝הֶ֗ם לֹ֣א נוֹתָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] waters covered their foes; one of them was not left.

en.L: And the waters covered their foes; not one of them was left.
en.B: The waters closed over their enemies; not a single one remained.
en.R: Every one of their enemies drowned under the water.

decisions.reason: The waters returned and covered the chariots and horsemen; not one of them remained (Exodus 14:28).

source.text: וַיַּאֲמִ֥ינוּ בִדְבָרָ֑יו יָ֝שִׁ֗ירוּ תְּהִלָּתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they believed in his words; they sang his praise.

en.L: Then they believed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words; they sang {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} praise.
en.B: Then they trusted {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promises and sang songs of praise to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Then the people believed what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had said, and they sang praises to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: faith and song after the crossing
decisions.reason: When Israel saw what the LORD had done, they believed in him and in his servant Moses, and then they sang (Exodus 14:31; 15:1).

decisions.choice: his words: what he had said
decisions.reason: His words are his promises to save them (Exodus 14:13-14).

source.text: מִֽ֭הֲרוּ שָׁכְח֣וּ מַעֲשָׂ֑יו לֹֽא־חִ֝כּ֗וּ לַעֲצָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: They hurried; they forgot his works; they did not wait for his counsel.

en.L: They hurried, they forgot {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} works; they did not wait for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} counsel.
en.B: How quickly they forgot {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} deeds! They would not wait to hear what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} intended.
en.R: Very soon they forgot the things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done. They did not wait to see what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} planned for them.

decisions.choice: they hurried, they forgot: they soon forgot
decisions.reason: Two verbs side by side make one idea: they were quick to forget.
Three days after the song at the sea the people grumbled at Marah, and soon after they longed for the food of Egypt (Exodus 15:22-24; 16:2-3).
The word ('etsah) is God's plan for them, which they would not wait to see unfold.

source.text: וַיִּתְאַוּ֣וּ תַ֭אֲוָה בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וַיְנַסּוּ־אֵ֝֗ל בִּֽישִׁימֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And they craved a craving in the wilderness, and they tested God in the wasteland.

en.L: And they craved with craving in the wilderness, and tested God in the wasteland.
en.B: Out in the wilderness their cravings ran wild, and in the wasteland they challenged God.
en.R: In the desert they wanted more and more food. They tested God to see what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would do.

decisions.reason: The people craved meat and wept for the food of Egypt (Numbers 11:4-6); the place was named Kibroth-hattaavah, "graves of craving", from the same word (Numbers 11:34).
To test God (nissah) is to demand that he prove himself instead of trusting him (Exodus 17:2, 7; Deuteronomy 6:16; 78:18).
The verb with its own noun makes it strong: their craving was intense.
Readable names what they craved (m1).

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לָ֭הֶם שֶׁאֱלָתָ֑ם וַיְשַׁלַּ֖ח רָז֣וֹן בְּנַפְשָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he gave to them their request, and he sent leanness into their soul.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them their request, and sent leanness into their souls.
en.B: He granted what they demanded, but with it {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent a disease that wasted them away.
en.R: He gave them what they wanted, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also made them sick and thin.

decisions.reason: God sent quail, but while the meat was still in their mouths he struck the people with a great plague (Numbers 11:31-33).
The word (razon) is thinness or wasting (Isaiah 10:16). The ancient Greek translation reads "fullness", taking the line as their being sick of the meat (Numbers 11:20).

decisions.choice: their soul: themselves, perhaps their throats
decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) is the self; with food in view it may also be the throat that craved.
Balanced and Readable say "them" for nefesh, the whole person.

source.text: וַיְקַנְא֣וּ לְ֭מֹשֶׁה בַּֽמַּחֲנֶ֑ה לְ֝אַהֲרֹ֗ן קְד֣וֹשׁ יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they were jealous of Moses in the camp, of Aaron, [the] holy one of YHWH.

en.L: And they were jealous of Moses in the camp, of Aaron, the holy one of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: They turned jealous of Moses there in the camp, and of Aaron, the man set apart as holy to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: In the camp, some people became jealous of Moses and of Aaron, the priest {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had set apart for {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}}.

decisions.choice: the rebellion of Korah, Dathan and Abiram
decisions.reason: Korah, Dathan and Abiram rose against Moses and Aaron, saying they had raised themselves above the LORD's people (Numbers 16).

decisions.choice: the holy one of the LORD: Aaron, consecrated as priest
decisions.reason: Aaron was set apart as priest; in Numbers 16 the LORD shows whom he has chosen as holy.
Readable makes plain that a group rose against them and that Aaron's holiness was his priesthood (m2).

source.text: תִּפְתַּח־אֶ֭רֶץ וַתִּבְלַ֣ע דָּתָ֑ן וַ֝תְּכַ֗ס עַל־עֲדַ֥ת אֲבִירָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] earth opened and swallowed Dathan, and covered over [the] company of Abiram.

en.L: The earth opened and swallowed Dathan, and covered over the company of Abiram.
en.B: The ground split open and swallowed Dathan; it closed over Abiram and his followers.
en.R: The ground opened up and swallowed Dathan. It closed over Abiram and his group.

decisions.reason: The ground split open and swallowed the rebels and their households, and the earth closed over them (Numbers 16). Deuteronomy 11:6 also names only Dathan and Abiram; Numbers 26:9-11 adds that the sons of Korah did not die.
The word ('edah) is an assembly; here the band that followed Abiram.

source.text: וַתִּבְעַר־אֵ֥שׁ בַּעֲדָתָ֑ם לֶ֝הָבָ֗ה תְּלַהֵ֥ט רְשָׁעִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And a fire burned among their company; a flame set ablaze [the] wicked.

en.L: And fire blazed among their company; flame burned up the wicked.
en.B: Then fire flared up in their company, and flames devoured the wicked.
en.R: A fire started among their group, and the flames burned up those wicked people.

decisions.reason: Fire came out from the LORD and consumed the two hundred and fifty men who offered incense with Korah (Numbers 16).
Readable makes clear that the wicked are the rebels just named.

source.text: יַעֲשׂוּ־עֵ֥גֶל בְּחֹרֵ֑ב וַ֝יִּשְׁתַּחֲו֗וּ לְמַסֵּכָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: They made a calf at Horeb, and bowed down to a cast image.

en.L: They made a calf at Horeb and bowed down to a cast image.
en.B: They made a calf at Horeb and bowed low before an idol of molten metal.
en.R: At Mount Sinai they made a gold statue of a calf and bowed down to worship it.

decisions.reason: While Moses was on the mountain, Aaron made a calf of gold, and the people worshiped it (Exodus 32:1-8; Deuteronomy 9:8-16).
Horeb is another name for the mountain of God, Sinai (Exodus 3:1; Deuteronomy 5:2).

decisions.choice: cast image: an idol of poured metal
decisions.reason: The word (massekhah) is an image made by pouring molten metal into a mold, the word used of the calf (Exodus 32:4, 8).
Readable uses the better-known name and says what the image was (m2, m3).

source.text: וַיָּמִ֥ירוּ אֶת־כְּבוֹדָ֑ם בְּתַבְנִ֥ית שׁ֝֗וֹר אֹכֵ֥ל עֵֽשֶׂב׃

records.literal_gloss: And they exchanged their glory for [the] image of an ox eating grass.

en.L: And they exchanged their glory for the image of an ox that eats grass.
en.B: They traded God, their glory, for the figure of a grass-eating bull.
en.R: They traded the glorious God they worshiped for a statue of a bull that eats grass!

decisions.reason: Israel's glory was the God who lived among them; they gave him up for an image (Jeremiah 2:11).
Paul echoes this verse: people exchanged the glory of the immortal God for images of humans and animals (Romans 1:23).

decisions.choice: an ox that eats grass: the folly of idols
decisions.reason: The words mock the idol: they traded the living God for the image of an animal that eats grass.
Balanced and Readable say who their glory was (m1).

source.text: שָׁ֭כְחוּ אֵ֣ל מוֹשִׁיעָ֑ם עֹשֶׂ֖ה גְדֹל֣וֹת בְּמִצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: They forgot God their savior, [who had] done great [things] in Egypt,

en.L: They forgot God their Savior, who had done great things in Egypt,
en.B: They forgot God their Savior and the great deeds {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had worked in Egypt,
en.R: They forgot God, who had saved them. They forgot the great things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done in Egypt.

decisions.reason: To forget God is not only a lapse of memory but turning from him (Deuteronomy 8:11-14; 78:11).
The word here is 'El, God, as in verse 14.

source.text: נִ֭פְלָאוֹת בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חָ֑ם נ֝וֹרָא֗וֹת עַל־יַם־סֽוּף׃

records.literal_gloss: wonders in [the] land of Ham, awesome [things] at [the] Sea of Reeds.

en.L: wonders in the land of Ham, awesome things by the Sea of Reeds.
en.B: wonders in the land of Ham, fearsome acts at the Red Sea.
en.R: He did amazing things in Egypt, the land of Ham, and terrifying things at the Red Sea.

decisions.reason: Egypt is called the land of Ham, after the father of Mizraim, that is, Egypt (Genesis 10:6; 105:23).

decisions.choice: awesome: deeds that make people afraid
decisions.reason: The word (nora'ot) is used of acts that fill people with awe and fear (Deuteronomy 10:21).

decisions.choice: the Sea of Reeds: the sea Israel crossed, known as the Red Sea
decisions.reason: The name (yam suf) means "sea of reeds". It is the sea of the crossing (Exodus 15:4, 22). The ancient Greek translation calls it the Red Sea, the name long used for it.
Balanced and Readable use the familiar name, as in Exodus; Literal translates the Hebrew name, "Sea of Reeds".

source.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר לְֽהַשְׁמִ֫ידָ֥ם לוּלֵ֡י מֹ֘שֶׁ֤ה בְחִיר֗וֹ עָמַ֣ד בַּפֶּ֣רֶץ לְפָנָ֑יו לְהָשִׁ֥יב חֲ֝מָת֗וֹ מֵֽהַשְׁחִֽית׃

records.literal_gloss: And he said to destroy them, had not Moses his chosen one stood in the breach before him to turn back his wrath from destroying.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said [{{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would] destroy them, had not Moses, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chosen one, stood in the breach before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to turn back {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wrath from destroying [them].
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would wipe them out; but Moses, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} chosen one, stood in the gap before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to turn {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger away so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would not destroy them.
en.R: So God said that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would destroy them. But Moses, the man {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had chosen, stood between {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and the people, like a soldier in a broken wall. Moses begged God to turn away {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger and not destroy them.

decisions.reason: After the calf the LORD said he would destroy the people, but Moses pleaded and the LORD relented (Exodus 32:9-14; Deuteronomy 9:13-14, 25-29).

decisions.choice: stood in the breach: put himself in the gap
decisions.reason: A soldier stands in a gap broken in a city wall to keep the enemy out (Ezekiel 13:5; 22:30). Moses stood between the people and God's anger.

decisions.choice: had not Moses: the destruction did not happen
decisions.reason: The word (lule) means "if not": God would have destroyed them, if Moses had not stood in the breach.

decisions.choice: God; like a soldier in a broken wall; Moses begged God
decisions.reason: Readable names who acts and spells out the picture (m2).

source.text: וַֽ֭יִּמְאֲסוּ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ חֶמְדָּ֑ה לֹֽא־הֶ֝אֱמִ֗ינוּ לִדְבָרֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they despised [the] land of desire; they did not believe his word,

en.L: And they despised the desirable land; they did not believe {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} word,
en.B: They looked down on the land of delight and put no faith in what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had promised,
en.R: Later they refused to go into the beautiful land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was giving them. They did not believe {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} promise.

decisions.choice: the spies and the refusal to enter
decisions.reason: When the spies brought a bad report, the people refused to go into Canaan and would not trust the LORD (Numbers 13-14; 14:11). God said their children would know the land they had "despised" (Numbers 14:31).

decisions.choice: the land of desire: a delightful land
decisions.reason: The phrase (erets chemdah) is a land to be longed for (Jeremiah 3:19; Zechariah 7:14).
Readable says how they showed their contempt (m1).

source.text: וַיֵּרָגְנ֥וּ בְאָהֳלֵיהֶ֑ם לֹ֥א שָׁ֝מְע֗וּ בְּק֣וֹל יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they grumbled in their tents; they did not listen to [the] voice of YHWH.

en.L: And they grumbled in their tents; they did not listen to the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: They muttered in their tents and would not heed the voice of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: They sat in their tents and complained. They would not obey {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.reason: After the spies' report the people grumbled against Moses and Aaron (Numbers 14:1-4); Moses later recalls, "you grumbled in your tents" (Deuteronomy 1:27), with the same verb.
To listen to someone's voice is to do what he says.
Readable says what listening means here (m2).

source.text: וַיִּשָּׂ֣א יָד֣וֹ לָהֶ֑ם לְהַפִּ֥יל א֝וֹתָ֗ם בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he raised his hand to them, to make them fall in the wilderness,

en.L: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lifted {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand to them, to make them fall in the wilderness,
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raised {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand in an oath that they would die in the wilderness,
en.R: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raised {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and made a solemn promise: they would die in the desert.

decisions.choice: raised his hand: swore an oath
decisions.reason: Raising the hand was the gesture of an oath (Exodus 6:8; Deuteronomy 32:40). God swore that the generation that refused the land would not enter it.

decisions.choice: the generation that died in the wilderness
decisions.reason: God said, "your dead bodies shall fall in this wilderness" (Numbers 14:28-35).

decisions.choice: make them fall: let them die
decisions.reason: "Fall" is a common way of saying die, in battle or by judgment.

source.text: וּלְהַפִּ֣יל זַ֭רְעָם בַּגּוֹיִ֑ם וּ֝לְזָרוֹתָ֗ם בָּאֲרָצֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: and to make their offspring fall among the nations, and to scatter them in the lands.

en.L: and to make their offspring fall among the nations, and to scatter them in the lands.
en.B: and that their children would be brought down among the nations and scattered through foreign lands.
en.R: He also swore that their descendants would die among other nations and be scattered all over the world.

decisions.choice: a warning that looks ahead to the exile
decisions.reason: The oath reaches beyond the wilderness to the scattering of Israel among the nations, as the law had warned (Leviticus 26:33; Deuteronomy 28:64). Verse 47 prays to be gathered back.
The Hebrew repeats "to make fall" from verse 26. The Syriac translation reads "to scatter", a word that looks much the same in Hebrew, as in the similar oath of Ezekiel 20.
Readable ended verse 26 with a full stop and repeats the oath here.

source.text: וַ֭יִּצָּ֣מְדוּ לְבַ֣עַל פְּע֑וֹר וַ֝יֹּאכְל֗וּ זִבְחֵ֥י מֵתִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And they joined themselves to Baal of Peor and ate sacrifices of [the] dead.

en.L: And they yoked themselves to Baal of Peor, and ate sacrifices of the dead.
en.B: They bound themselves to the Baal of Peor and ate offerings made to the dead.
en.R: They joined in worshiping the god Baal at Peor. They ate meat sacrificed to dead gods.

decisions.reason: At Shittim the men of Israel joined in the feasts of Moab's gods and "yoked themselves to the Baal of Peor", the same verb (Numbers 25:1-3).

decisions.choice: sacrifices of the dead: offerings to lifeless gods
decisions.reason: The dead may be the idols, which have no life, in contrast to the living God; or the line may mean meals offered for the dead.

decisions.choice: Baal of Peor: the Baal worshiped at Peor
decisions.reason: Baal ("lord") was a name for Canaanite gods; this one was worshiped at Mount Peor in Moab (Numbers 23:28).
Readable follows the first sense in m2.

source.text: וַ֭יַּכְעִיסוּ בְּמַֽעַלְלֵיהֶ֑ם וַתִּפְרָץ־בָּ֝֗ם מַגֵּפָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they provoked [him] by their deeds, and a plague broke out among them.

en.L: And they provoked [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] to anger with their deeds, and a plague broke out among them.
en.B: They made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} angry by what they did, and plague burst out among them.
en.R: What they did made God angry, and a terrible sickness spread among them.

decisions.reason: The LORD's anger burned against Israel, and twenty-four thousand died in the plague (Numbers 25:3, 9).
The verb has no object; God is meant (verse 32 is the same).
Readable names whom they angered (m2).

source.text: וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד פִּֽ֭ינְחָס וַיְפַלֵּ֑ל וַ֝תֵּעָצַ֗ר הַמַּגֵּפָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And Phinehas stood up and intervened, and the plague was restrained.

en.L: And Phinehas stood up and intervened, and the plague was restrained.
en.B: Then Phinehas rose and stepped in, and the plague was halted.
en.R: But Phinehas took action, and the plague stopped.

decisions.reason: Phinehas the priest, Aaron's grandson, killed an Israelite man and a Midianite woman in the act, and the plague was stopped (Numbers 25:7-8).
The verb (pillel) is to judge or arbitrate, to step in between parties (1 Samuel 2:25). Here he acts as judge; Numbers 25:13 says he "made atonement" for Israel.

source.text: וַתֵּחָ֣שֶׁב ל֭וֹ לִצְדָקָ֑ה לְדֹ֥ר וָ֝דֹ֗ר עַד־עוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was counted to him as righteousness, to generation and generation, until forever.

en.L: And it was counted to him as righteousness, to generation and generation, forever.
en.B: And that deed was counted to him as righteousness for all generations, for all time.
en.R: Because of this, God counted him as righteous for all time to come.

decisions.reason: The words recall Abraham, whose faith the LORD "counted to him as righteousness" (Genesis 15:6). Phinehas was given a covenant of lasting priesthood (Numbers 25:11-13).

decisions.choice: to generation and generation: for all time
decisions.reason: The doubled word means every generation to come.
Readable names who counted it.

source.text: וַ֭יַּקְצִיפוּ עַל־מֵ֥י מְרִיבָ֑ה וַיֵּ֥רַע לְ֝מֹשֶׁ֗ה בַּעֲבוּרָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they provoked [him] at [the] waters of Meribah, and it went badly for Moses on account of them,

en.L: And they made [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] angry at the waters of Meribah, and it went badly for Moses because of them,
en.B: At the waters of Meribah they made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} angry, and Moses paid dearly because of them,
en.R: At the springs of Meribah they made God angry, and Moses got into trouble because of them.

decisions.reason: At Kadesh the people quarreled with Moses for water; Moses struck the rock, and God told him he would not lead the people into the land (Numbers 20:2-13; Deuteronomy 1:37; 3:26).
The verb has no object; God is meant, as in verse 29, though Moses too was provoked.
The name means quarreling or dispute (95:8).
Readable names whom they angered (m2).

source.text: כִּֽי־הִמְר֥וּ אֶת־רוּח֑וֹ וַ֝יְבַטֵּ֗א בִּשְׂפָתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: for they rebelled against his spirit, and he spoke rashly with his lips.

en.L: for they rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit, and he spoke rashly with his lips.
en.B: for they defied {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} Spirit, and Moses let hasty words pass his lips.
en.R: They rebelled against God's Spirit, and Moses said things he should not have said.

decisions.reason: The verb (himrah) is the word for rebelling against God used in verses 7 and 43, and Isaiah 63 speaks of Israel rebelling against God's Holy Spirit in the wilderness. Others take "his spirit" as Moses' spirit, which the people made bitter.
Moses said, "Listen, you rebels; must we bring water for you out of this rock?" and struck it (Numbers 20:10-12).
Balanced and Readable name who spoke rashly, since "his" has just meant God.
Readable names whose Spirit, as taken in m1.

source.text: לֹֽא־הִ֭שְׁמִידוּ אֶת־הָֽעַמִּ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֤ר אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה לָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: They did not destroy the peoples which YHWH said to them,

en.L: They did not destroy the peoples, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had said to them,
en.B: They did not wipe out the peoples {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told them to destroy,
en.R: When they entered the land, they did not destroy the nations there, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded.

decisions.choice: the peoples left in the land
decisions.reason: The tribes did not drive out the peoples of Canaan (Judges 1:21-36), and the LORD's messenger rebuked them at Bochim (Judges 2:1-3).

decisions.choice: the command to destroy the peoples
decisions.reason: The law commanded Israel to destroy the peoples of Canaan so that Israel would not learn to worship their gods (Deuteronomy 7:1-5; 20:18). The psalm does not soften the command; it shows what came of ignoring it (verses 35-39).
Readable marks the move from the wilderness to Canaan.

source.text: וַיִּתְעָרְב֥וּ בַגּוֹיִ֑ם וַֽ֝יִּלְמְד֗וּ מַֽעֲשֵׂיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: and they mixed themselves with the nations and learned their deeds,

en.L: and they mingled with the nations and learned their deeds,
en.B: instead they mixed with the nations and took up their ways.
en.R: Instead, they mixed with those nations and learned to live like them.

decisions.reason: Israel lived among the peoples of Canaan, married their daughters and served their gods (Judges 3:5-6).
The verb (hit'arev) is to mix oneself in, to join a people, including by marriage (Ezra 9:2).

source.text: וַיַּעַבְד֥וּ אֶת־עֲצַבֵּיהֶ֑ם וַיִּהְי֖וּ לָהֶ֣ם לְמוֹקֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: and they served their idols, and they became for them a snare.

en.L: and they served their idols, and they became a snare to them.
en.B: They served those nations' idols, which turned into a trap for them.
en.R: They worshiped the idols of those nations, and those idols trapped them.

decisions.reason: The law warned that the gods of the peoples would be a snare to Israel (Deuteronomy 7:16), and so it was (Judges 2:3, 11-13).

decisions.choice: a snare: a trap that catches
decisions.reason: A snare is a bird trap; the idols drew Israel in and held them.
Balanced and Readable make clear whose idols they were.

source.text: וַיִּזְבְּח֣וּ אֶת־בְּ֭נֵיהֶם וְאֶת־בְּנֽוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם לַשֵּֽׁדִים׃

records.literal_gloss: And they sacrificed their sons and their daughters to the demons.

en.L: And they sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons.
en.B: They even offered up their own sons and daughters to demons.
en.R: They even killed their own sons and daughters as sacrifices to demons.

decisions.choice: demons: the powers behind the idols
decisions.reason: The word (shedim) is used only here and in Deuteronomy 32:17, where Israel sacrificed "to demons, not to God". The idols of verse 36 stand for spiritual powers that are not God.
The law forbade giving children to Molech (Leviticus 18:21), and the prophets condemned the burning of children in the valley of Hinnom (Jeremiah 7:31; 19:5).
Balanced and Readable mark this as the depth of Israel's sin.

source.text: וַיִּֽשְׁפְּכ֨וּ דָ֪ם נָקִ֡י דַּם־בְּנֵ֘יהֶ֤ם וּֽבְנוֹתֵיהֶ֗ם אֲשֶׁ֣ר זִ֭בְּחוּ לַעֲצַבֵּ֣י כְנָ֑עַן וַתֶּחֱנַ֥ף הָ֝אָ֗רֶץ בַּדָּמִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And they shed innocent blood, [the] blood of their sons and their daughters whom they sacrificed to [the] idols of Canaan, and the land was polluted with the blood[shed].

en.L: And they shed innocent blood, the blood of their sons and their daughters, whom they sacrificed to the idols of Canaan, and the land was polluted with blood.
en.B: They spilled the blood of the innocent, their own sons and daughters, slaughtered as offerings to Canaan's idols, and the land was made unclean by bloodshed.
en.R: They killed innocent children, their own sons and daughters, as sacrifices to the idols of Canaan. Their blood made the land unclean.

decisions.reason: The verb (chanaf) is used in Numbers 35:33: bloodshed pollutes the land, and only the blood of the killer can make atonement for it.
The plural of the word for blood means blood that has been shed, killing.
Shedding innocent blood is the sin named against Manasseh, for which Judah was sent into exile (Jeremiah 19:4; 2 Kings 24:4).

source.text: וַיִּטְמְא֥וּ בְמַעֲשֵׂיהֶ֑ם וַ֝יִּזְנוּ֗בְּמַֽעַלְלֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they became unclean by their works, and they prostituted themselves by their deeds.

en.L: And they became unclean by their works, and played the prostitute by their deeds.
en.B: They made themselves unclean by what they did and were unfaithful like a prostitute in their ways.
en.R: What they did made them unclean. They were unfaithful to God, like a wife who sleeps with other men.

decisions.choice: prostituted themselves: were unfaithful to God
decisions.reason: Worship of other gods is pictured as a wife's unfaithfulness, since Israel was bound to the LORD by covenant (Exodus 34:15-16; Judges 2:17).

decisions.choice: became unclean: unfit to come before God
decisions.reason: The verb (tame') is the word for ritual uncleanness; here it is caused by idolatry and bloodshed (Leviticus 18:24-25).

decisions.choice: unfaithful to God, like a wife who sleeps with other men
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m1).

source.text: וַיִּֽחַר־אַ֣ף יְהוָ֣ה בְּעַמּ֑וֹ וַ֝יְתָעֵ֗ב אֶת־נַחֲלָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And [the] anger of YHWH burned against his people, and he abhorred his inheritance.

en.L: And the anger of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} abhorred {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} inheritance.
en.B: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} burned with anger against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people and came to loathe {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own possession.
en.R: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} became very angry with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people. He was disgusted with the people who belonged to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.reason: "The anger of the LORD burned against Israel, and he gave them into the hands of plunderers" is the refrain of Judges (Judges 2:14, 20; 3:8; 10:7). Verses 40-46 sum up that whole period.
The verb (ti'ev) is used of what is detestable. God's own people had become hateful to him by their idols; yet verse 45 says he remembered his covenant.
As in verse 5, Israel is God's possession.

source.text: וַיִּתְּנֵ֥ם בְּיַד־גּוֹיִ֑ם וַֽיִּמְשְׁל֥וּ בָ֝הֶ֗ם שֹׂנְאֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he gave them into [the] hand of nations, and those who hated them ruled over them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them into the hand of nations, and those who hated them ruled over them.
en.B: He handed them over to other nations, and people who hated them became their masters.
en.R: He let other nations take control of them. People who hated them ruled over them.

decisions.choice: given into the hand of nations
decisions.reason: God gave Israel into the hand of Cushan-rishathaim, Eglon of Moab, Jabin of Canaan, Midian and others (Judges 3:8, 12-14; 4:2; 6:1; 10:7).

decisions.choice: into the hand: into the power
decisions.reason: As in verse 10, the hand means power.

source.text: וַיִּלְחָצ֥וּם אוֹיְבֵיהֶ֑ם וַ֝יִּכָּנְע֗וּ תַּ֣חַת יָדָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And their enemies oppressed them, and they were humbled under their hand.

en.L: And their enemies oppressed them, and they were brought low under their hand.
en.B: Their enemies crushed them and forced them to bow under their power.
en.R: Their enemies treated them cruelly and forced them to obey.

decisions.reason: Jabin oppressed Israel harshly for twenty years (Judges 4:3); the Ammonites crushed them for eighteen (Judges 10:8).
The verb (nikhna') is to be brought low, used of enemies subdued (Judges 3:30; 8:28).

source.text: פְּעָמִ֥ים רַבּ֗וֹת יַצִּ֫ילֵ֥ם וְ֭הֵמָּה יַמְר֣וּ בַעֲצָתָ֑ם וַ֝יָּמֹ֗כּוּ בַּעֲוֺנָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Many times he delivered them, but they rebelled in their counsel, and they sank low in their iniquity.

en.L: Many times {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} delivered them, but they rebelled in their counsel, and they sank low in their iniquity.
en.B: Again and again {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rescued them, but they kept to their own rebellious plans and sank down in their sin.
en.R: Time after time {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set them free, but they kept choosing to turn against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Their sins dragged them down.

decisions.choice: the judges and the people's relapses
decisions.reason: God raised up judges who saved Israel, but when each judge died the people turned back to worse ways (Judges 2:16-19).
The word ('etsah) is a plan; they followed their own counsel instead of waiting for God's (verse 13).
The verb (makhakh) is to sink or become low; their sin brought them down.

source.text: וַ֭יַּרְא בַּצַּ֣ר לָהֶ֑ם בְּ֝שָׁמְע֗וֹ אֶת־רִנָּתָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he looked on the distress of them, when he heard their cry.

en.L: Yet {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} looked on their distress when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heard their cry.
en.B: Even so, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw the trouble they were in when their cry reached {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: But when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heard them crying out for help, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw how much they were suffering.

decisions.reason: In Judges the LORD was moved by the groaning of his people (Judges 2:18; 10:16), as he had heard their cry in Egypt (Exodus 2:23-25; 3:7).

decisions.choice: cry: a loud cry, here a plea
decisions.reason: The word (rinnah) is usually a ringing shout of joy (105:43); here it is a loud cry for help (17:1; 61:2).
The simple "and" joins God's mercy to Israel's rebellion; the sense is "yet", as in verse 8.

source.text: וַיִּזְכֹּ֣ר לָהֶ֣ם בְּרִית֑וֹ וַ֝יִּנָּחֵ֗ם כְּרֹ֣ב חֲסָדָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he remembered for them his covenant, and he relented according to the abundance of his loyal loves.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} remembered {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant for them, and relented according to the abundance of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love.
en.B: For their sake {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called to mind {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant and turned from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger, because {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} loyal love is so great.
en.R: He remembered {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant with them. Because {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} faithful love is so great, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} decided not to punish them as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had planned.

decisions.reason: The Hebrew text notes a difference here between what is written and what is to be read; the words follow the form to be read, "his loyal loves" (plural).

decisions.choice: relented: turned from the judgment he had announced
decisions.reason: The verb (nicham) is used when God turns from a judgment he had threatened (Exodus 32:14). It does not mean that God is fickle; his loyal love moves him to mercy.
The law promised that when the people were in their enemies' land God would remember his covenant (Leviticus 26:42, 45). The words recall 105:8 and 42.
The word (chesed) is the love that keeps faith, God's commitment to his people that does not give up (5:8).
As in the earlier psalms, Readable says "faithful love" for chesed.

decisions.choice: decided not to punish them as he had planned
decisions.reason: Readable says what relenting means here (m2).

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן אוֹתָ֣ם לְרַחֲמִ֑ים לִ֝פְנֵ֗י כָּל־שׁוֹבֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he gave them to compassion before all their captors.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made them [objects of] compassion before all their captors.
en.B: He moved all those who had carried them off to treat them with pity.
en.R: He made the people who had taken them away as prisoners feel sorry for them.

decisions.reason: Solomon prayed that God would grant his exiled people compassion before their captors (1 Kings 8:50). God did so in the days of Ezra and Nehemiah (Ezra 9:9; Nehemiah 1:11).

decisions.choice: gave them to compassion: caused others to pity them
decisions.reason: To "give someone to compassion before" others is to make those others show them mercy.

source.text: הוֹשִׁיעֵ֨נוּ׀יְה֘וָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֗ינוּ וְקַבְּצֵנוּ֮ מִֽן־הַגּ֫וֹיִ֥ם לְ֭הֹדוֹת לְשֵׁ֣ם קָדְשֶׁ֑ךָ לְ֝הִשְׁתַּבֵּ֗חַ בִּתְהִלָּתֶֽךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: Save us, YHWH our God, and gather us from the nations, to give thanks to [the] name of your holiness, to boast in your praise.

en.L: Save us, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God, and gather us from the nations, to give thanks to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy name, to glory in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise.
en.B: Rescue us, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God, and bring us back together from among the nations, so that we may thank {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy name and make our boast in praising {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.R: Save us, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God! Bring us back home from the other nations. Then we will thank {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, the holy God, and proudly sing {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} praise.

decisions.reason: Verses 47-48 close the song in 1 Chronicles 16 (16:35-36), which begins "Say, save us, God of our salvation" and adds "deliver us".

decisions.choice: gather us from the nations: a prayer from exile
decisions.reason: The prayer is spoken by a people still scattered (verse 27). The law promised that if they returned to the LORD he would gather them from all the peoples (Deuteronomy 30:3-4).
The verb (hishtabbeach) is to boast or take pride; their boast will be in praising God.

source.text: בָּר֤וּךְ־יְהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵ֪י יִשְׂרָאֵ֡ל מִן־הָ֤עוֹלָ֨ם׀וְעַ֬ד הָעוֹלָ֗ם וְאָמַ֖ר כָּל־הָעָ֥ם אָמֵ֗ן הַֽלְלוּ־יָֽהּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Blessed [be] YHWH, [the] God of Israel, from the everlasting and until the everlasting. And let all the people say, Amen. Praise Yah.

en.L: Blessed [be] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting! And let all the people say, "Amen." Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}.
en.B: May {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, be blessed from ages past to ages to come! And let all the people answer, "Amen!" Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!
en.R: Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel! He has always been worthy of praise, and always will be. Let everyone say, "Amen!" Praise {{divine_name:the LORD|Yah}}!

decisions.reason: This blessing ends Book Four of the Psalms (Psalms 90-106), as 41:14, 72:18-19 and 89:53 end the first three books. Book Five opens with Psalm 107. The blessing closes the whole book as well as this psalm.
The song in 1 Chronicles 16 ends with this blessing, and adds that all the people said "Amen" and praised the LORD (16:36).
Amen ('amen) is a word of agreement: "it is true, so be it". The people make the blessing their own.

decisions.choice: from everlasting to everlasting: for all time, past and future
decisions.reason: The word ('olam) is the farthest time, before or ahead; the pair means always (41:14; 90:2).

The cry "Hallelu-yah" is a command to a group, "praise", with Yah, the short form of the divine name YHWH (as in Exodus 15:2). It is rendered "Praise the LORD", with Yah as the alternative for the name.
